item.title: Harsha Venkayalapti
item.description: Date: January 13th, 2026 Focus: dealing with burnout, deep work optimization and recovery strategies Experiment with the 90-second morning work protocol, if possible Track deep work sessions and note duration/quality Cut out low-leverage work ruthlessly by applying the Pareto Principle Focus on active recovery, use the body to quell the mind Practice NSDR or walking between sessions (no phone) Try stress management (like Yoga or Tai Chi) Hit the sauna specifically for recovery Experiment with caffeine intake (delay 1-2 hours post-wake) Add one Norwegian 4x4 session this week Try one Zone 2 session (different day) or REHIT if time-constrained Looking forward to hearing how it goes!Your dopamine availability is highest when you first wake up, these stores are essentially "set" for the day. This is also when you're most prone to entering flow states. Feel free to do this after your Sadhana practice. The 90-Second Rule: Start your hardest cognitive task within 90 seconds of waking. Here's why this works: Your memory and habitual thought patterns take time to fully "instantiate" after sleep Before they load in, you can approach problems with fresh eyes and heightened creativity This window is when your brain is neurologically primed for novel thinking Alternative approach: If diving straight into 90 minutes feels too intense, try 15-20 minutes of focused work, then a quick 10-minute walk (morning sunlight helps set your circadian rhythm), then continue your deep work sprint. SAD Lamp: Since you consistently wake up at 4 am and the sun usually isn't out yet, consider purchasing a SAD lamp (this is the one I use). Feel free to look at their other offerings, they have a few different types, or if this is expensive find a different brand, 10000 Lux is the most important part. The mechanism involves: Circadian regulation: Light exposure suppresses melatonin production and helps reset your circadian clock Neurotransmitter modulation: Bright light influences serotonin synthesis and may affect dopamine pathways Retinal photoreceptors: Specialized cells (intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells) detect light intensity and send signals to the brain's suprachiasmatic nucleus, your biological clock The 90-Minute Sprint: Work in focused blocks of up to 90 minutes, aligned with your brain's natural ultradian rhythm. Finding Your Duration: Experiment to find your ideal sprint length. Use energy levels or subjective mental fatigue as your guide, 90 minutes is the ceiling, not the requirement. Volume: Start with 2-3 deep work sessions per day. You can scale up to 5 if necessary, but note that even elite performers who've practiced extensively tend to max out at 5 sessions. Recovery Between Sessions: NSDR (Non-Sleep Deep Rest): Triggers neural replay and accelerates memory consolidation, your brain is literally processing and encoding what you just worked on Go for a walk (touch grass): Resets your neurochemistry and restores cognitive resources Avoid: Scrolling on your phone. This drains dopamine availability rather than restoring it. The goal during recovery is replenishment, not stimulation. Most CEO burnout comes from high-effort, low-leverage work. The goal isn't just finding what you're good at, it's finding what only you can do that creates disproportionate value, then ruthlessly cutting everything else. Track energy drain too, some "valuable" tasks might need delegation if they're personally depleting. Sustainable performance > grinding through everything.1. Track & Categorize (1 week minimum) Log every task/meeting with time spent Note energy level for each (high/medium/low drain) Categories might include: strategic planning, team management, client work, operations/admin, firefighting, etc. 2. Value Analysis For each category/task, assess: Revenue impact: Directly drives growth/retention? Strategic leverage: Moves critical initiatives forward? Unique value: Only I can do this effectively? 3. The 80/20 Cut Identify the ~20% of activities producing ~80% of value: These are "CEO-only" tasks (strategy, key relationships, vision-setting) Everything else is a candidate for elimination or delegation 4. Action Matrix Keep & protect: High-value, CEO-unique tasks → block time for these Delegate: Medium-value, others can do 70%+ as well → assign ownership Eliminate: Low-value, ceremonial, or habit-based → just stop Automate: Repetitive decisions → create frameworks/SOPs for team Delay your first caffeine by 1-2 hours after waking. This prevents interference with your natural cortisol awakening response and protects your sleep-wake cycle.Add dedicated sauna sessions: Schedule gym visits specifically for sauna/steam room use, separate from workouts. This re-frames recovery as active practice rather than an afterthought. Practice a dedicated yoga routine: Spend some time each day doing Yoga or Tai Chi to actively recover and manage your stressRapid heat stress method (for time-limited sessions): 10 minutes steam room first → suppresses sweating capacity, rapidly elevating core temperature 20 minutes dry sauna → sustained heat exposure at 170-190°F Traditional approach (more gradual): 20-30 minutes dry sauna at 170-190°F Multiple sessions per week (Scandinavian research shows benefits at 4-7x/week) Neurobiological effects: Endorphin/dynorphin system: Heat stress triggers beta-endorphin release (natural opioids), followed by dynorphin sensitivity changes that create lasting mood elevation and stress resilience BDNF elevation: Sauna increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor, supporting neuroplasticity and potentially offering antidepressant-like effects Heat shock proteins: HSPs provide neuroprotection and may reduce neuroinflammation associated with chronic stress Stress & recovery mechanisms: Cortisol regulation: Regular sauna use helps normalize HPA axis function, reducing chronic stress response Parasympathetic activation: Heat exposure followed by cooling creates strong parasympathetic shift, training stress recovery systems Sleep enhancement: Evening sauna improves sleep quality through core temperature manipulation (same principle as your 8sleep) Clinical data: Finnish studies show regular sauna users have significantly lower rates of depression, anxiety, and psychotic disorders. Effects appear dose-dependent—more frequent/longer sessions correlate with greater mental health benefits. The practice pairs well with cold exposure (Wim Hof work) for maximum hormetic stress adaptation. You're already doing daily resistance training with your trainer—excellent foundation. Adding strategic cardio will amplify your cognitive performance and energy levels. Norwegian 4x4 Protocol (Gold Standard) 4 intervals of 4 minutes at high intensity (85-95% max heart rate) 3 minutes active recovery between intervals Most effective protocol for cardiovascular health Performance hack: Can be used as a pre-meeting primer for important meetings—elevated cardiovascular state enhances cognitive sharpness Zone 2 Cardio (Base Building) 2 longer sessions per week (30-60 min) Conversational pace—you should be able to talk but not sing Builds aerobic base and improves VO2 max Schedule on different days than Norwegian 4x4 REHIT / CAROL Bike (Time-Efficient Option) For days when time is limited Extremely time-effective (~9 minutes total) Provides significant cardiovascular benefit with minimal time investment Cons: expensive investment costs around 2.5k We didn't get to cover this in our session, but here are the key conditions that increase your probability of entering flow states:Pre-Session Checklist: What specifically am I trying to accomplish? How will I know I'm making progress? Have I eliminated all possible distractions? Is this challenging enough to fully engage me?
